_README: W12b's channel pool. AUTHORED, NEVER INFERRED.
`channel_id` is the authority and `handle` is a convenience: handles change,
channel ids do not. Every id here is resolved once by
`python -m core.video.resolve_channels` against the YouTube Data API and
pasted in. A NULL id is not a placeholder to be filled in by guessing --
core.video.channels REFUSES to load an entry whose id is null or whose id
still looks like a handle, so the refresh path cannot run against a guess.
`accent` is authored on the CHANNEL, never detected from a video, and has
exactly two values by operator ruling (2026-08-30): two accents that are
actually rotated beat six with no channels behind them. Adding a third later
is a data change -- one value here and one literal in migration 019's CHECK.
A NULL accent is refused for the same reason a null id is.
`accent_null` DISCRIMINATES TWO STATES THAT A BARE NULL FLATTENS INTO ONE,
and it is REQUIRED whenever `accent` is null and FORBIDDEN when it is not --
enforced in both directions, so the two fields cannot drift apart.
by_ruling     -- no single value can be TRUE for this channel. Pollable:
the video is selectable and `accent_rotation` SKIPS it
rather than rotating on a value somebody invented.
REQUIRES `accent_null_reason`, a written sentence.
pending_check -- nobody has watched the channel yet. REFUSED by the
loader until an accent is authored or it is ruled.
The reason `by_ruling` requires a written reason is not tidiness: without
one it becomes the easy escape from watching a video, and `pending_check`
quietly empties into it. Operator ruling, 2026-09-01.
A SENTINEL VALUE IN `accent` -- "unknown", "many" -- WAS PROPOSED AND
REFUSED, and the refusal is recorded so it is not rediscovered as a tidy
idea. It would have to be admitted by migration 019's CHECK and stored in
the column, at which point it IS a third bucket and every future reader is
free to bucket it. That is #315 with a nicer spelling: it makes bucketing
the default and skipping the special case. The ruling is that a null is
SKIPPED -- never bucketed, never defaulted, never counted as exposure.
`track` uses the vocabulary of `users.track_weights` (migration 012) so that
`topic_match` compares like with like: life | curiosity | work.
PRODUCT-PRINCIPLES §3: this file is GLOBAL CONFIGURATION THAT BECOMES
PER-USER IF THE TWO LEARNERS' INTERESTS DIVERGE. Today both share the pool
and `users.track_weights` does the per-learner work. When it diverges it
gains a users-keyed table, not a second file.

RECORDED HERE BECAUSE A HANDLE CORRECTION AND A CHANNEL SUBSTITUTION ARE NOT
THE SAME EDIT.

It did not resolve: the Data API returned no

The channel is legitimate and the coverage score judges it on merit. But it

THE ACCENT IS NULL AND WAS NOT CARRIED OVER, WHICH IS A DECISION AND NOT AN
OVERSIGHT. The old entry was authored `british` for the BERLIN channel. That
value described a different channel, and this file's own rule is that
authoring an accent means knowing it -- a value inherited from a previous
occupant is exactly the plausible-but-unverified value the rule exists to
refuse. It costs nothing today (the null id already refuses the entry) and it
prevents an unverified accent going live the moment the id lands.
_POOL_BALANCE: The target is Life & Social 50 / Curiosity 30 / Work 20 (PRD §4.6).
BY AUTHORED CHANNEL COUNT THIS POOL IS 55 / 36 / 9, AND IT DOES NOT MEET THE
TARGET. THE 2026-08-31 ID RESOLUTION DID NOT CHANGE IT: the eleventh entry
stayed on the `life` track, so the authored split is unchanged.
WHAT DID CHANGE IS WHAT THE LOADER ACCEPTS, AND THAT IS THE NUMBER THAT
REACHES SELECTION. Before, every `channel_id` was null and the pool loaded
ZERO channels. Ten ids are now written, so SEVEN entries load: the other four
are refused, three for a null accent (Claire, Learn English With TV Series,
TED-Ed) and one for a null id (@easyenglish551).
loadable 2026-08-31: 7 of 11 -- life 3 / curiosity 3 / work 1 = 43/43/14
loadable 2026-09-01: 8 of 11 -- life 3 / curiosity 4 / work 1 = 37.5/50/12.5
EVERY channel_id IS NOW RESOLVED. @easyenglish551's landed on 2026-09-01
(UCTRHegh7UqWuKRymXoqzbzA), and THE SPLIT DID NOT MOVE: the entry is
still refused, on its accent instead of its id. What changed is that the
pool now has exactly ONE kind of blocker left and it is the same one for
all three refusals -- accent_null: pending_check. That is a person
watching three channels, not a lookup anybody can run.
Migration 020 made TED-Ed loadable as a by_ruling null accent. Claire and
Learn English With TV Series stay refused as pending_check, and
@easyenglish551 stays refused for its null id. CURIOSITY NOW OVERTAKES
LIFE and the loadable pool is FURTHER from the target than before, which
was predicted before the change and is not a regression: the weights are
scoring terms, not quotas.
So the pool that can actually be polled is FURTHER from 50/30/20 than the
authored one, and curiosity is level with life rather than behind it. Stated
here rather than discovered from the assignments.
That is recorded here rather than left to be discovered from the assignments.
It does not have to meet it, and the reason is worth stating so nobody
'fixes' it later: THE WEIGHTS ARE SCORING TERMS, NOT QUOTAS. `topic_match` is
one 0.20 term in a weighted sum (PRD §7.2); nothing enforces a ratio, and the
realised mix runs roughly channel-proportional. A slice that promised
50/30/20 and delivered 55/36/9 would be reporting a target as a result.
THE WORK TRACK HAS ONE CHANNEL, AND THEREFORE ONE ACCENT. So `accent_rotation`
(0.15) and `topic_match` (0.20) are structurally in conflict there: a work
video can only ever be British. Filed as a known issue with a target rather
than worked around here.

channels.name: English Teacher Claire
channels.why: Conversational everyday English at a deliberate pace; operator-approved as a Life & Social anchor.

channels.name: Friends (official)
channels.why: Real scripted conversation between friends -- the register PRD §4.6 exists to protect, and the one thing a teaching channel cannot supply.

channels.name: Easy English (scripted lessons)
channels.why: Everyday conversational English performed as short scripted dialogues. NOT the channel this entry was created for -- see _SUBSTITUTION below; it is kept on merit and scored like any other teaching channel.
channels._unresolved: accent only. The id was resolved on the host 2026-09-01 and this entry is now refused on ONE count instead of two. The accent is NOT carried over from the previous occupant of this entry -- see _SUBSTITUTION -- and it is pending_check rather than by_ruling: nobody has watched this channel, and it is not a channel that CANNOT have an accent.

channels.name: Learn English With TV Series
channels.why: Connected speech and reductions taught from real clips, which is PRD §7.5's stated failure mode for a learner with good grammar.

channels.name: Speak English With Vanessa
channels.why: Everyday phrases in full sentences at natural speed; a steady mid-B1 supply.

channels.name: Rachel's English
channels.why: Explicit General American pronunciation and reductions; the American half of the accent rotation.

channels.accent_null_reason: TED-Ed lessons are narrated by many different voices, so the channel HAS NO SINGLE ACCENT and a per-channel field cannot hold the truth about it. This is not uncertainty that watching would resolve.
channels.name: TED-Ed
channels.why: Short narrated explainers on one idea; dense but clearly structured, and the transcripts are unusually clean.
channels._unresolved: accent NOT AUTHORED -- see _UNRESOLVED below. TED-Ed is the structural case, not merely the uncertain one.

channels.name: Vox
channels.why: Explanatory journalism; real adult subject matter rather than material written for learners.

channels.name: Johnny Harris
channels.why: One narrator, strong narrative drive; holds attention through a longer runtime than the pool's average.

channels.name: BBC Learning English (News Review)
channels.why: Current news retold with the vocabulary made explicit; the British half of the accent rotation.

channels.name: English with Lucy
channels.why: The pool's only Work-track channel; formal register and British pronunciation.

_UNRESOLVED: THREE ACCENTS ARE DELIBERATELY NULL, AND THIS IS A FINDING RATHER THAN AN
OMISSION. `accent` is authored, and authoring it means knowing it -- writing
a plausible value would be the same defect as writing a plausible channel id.
@EnglishTeacherClaire     -- not established by the author of this file.
@LearnEnglishWithTVSeries -- not established by the author of this file.
@TEDEd -- NOT UNCERTAINTY BUT A STRUCTURAL MISMATCH. TED-Ed lessons are
narrated by many different voices, so the channel HAS NO SINGLE ACCENT and
a per-channel field cannot hold the truth about it. The three honest
options are: drop TED-Ed from the pool; author the accent per VIDEO for
this channel only (a schema change, since `videos.accent` is currently
copied from the channel); or accept a nominal value and know that
`accent_rotation` is lying by that much. THIS IS THE OPERATOR'S RULING TO
MAKE, and it is filed rather than chosen here.
@easyenglish551 -- ADDED 2026-08-31. Its accent is null because the entry
CHANGED CHANNEL and the previous occupant's authored `british` described a
different channel. See _SUBSTITUTION. This entry is refused on TWO counts,
a null id and a null accent, and both are the operator's to fill.
Until each is filled, core.video.channels refuses to load that entry and
`core.video.refresh` will not poll it; it does not silently run with a guess.
